Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're excited to get the Private (VPC) deployment kicked off. Before we schedule the ops kickoff, our infra team asked me to surface a few items so we can map gaps and have the right people on the call. High level ask: can Redwood confirm the minimum account and network pre-reqs you need so we can prepare evidence and access?

Top questions from our side:
- Which service accounts and roles do you need from our cloud tenancy (least privilege)?
- Preferred KMS model (customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS or Redwood-managed)?
- IP allowlist and egress requirements for model pull + artifact downloads (URLs/ports).
- Do you require a NAT or specific private endpoints for telemetry?
- Expected minimum bandwidth and concurrent connection counts for initial 1-node pilot.

We can attach our current network diagram and inventory. Attaching clearfield-network-diagram-v2.pdf.

Proposed attendees for kickoff: EngOps (me), Network lead (Raj), SecOps (Maya), Database (Sam). Let us know if Redwood needs additional attendees (SRE, CSM, procurement).

Thanks,

Clearfield Health

Hi Aaron — great to hear and thanks for sending the diagram. I pulled the checklist together below so your team can check boxes before the kickoff. I attached a runbook template (redwood-mip-runbook.xlsx) with fields we typically collect during intake.

Redwood preflight checklist (pilot scope: 1 dedicated node, VPC peering model):
1) Identity & Access
   - Create a service account for Redwood-integration@clearfield with the following minimal roles: Compute Viewer, Storage Object Viewer, KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter (if using customer-managed keys), and Logging Viewer.
   - Provide an OAuth client redirect URI for the admin console (if you plan to use the web UI).
2) Networking
   - Provide VPC ID and subnet IDs for private endpoints.
   - Ensure outbound access to: model-artifacts.redwood.ai (443), update.redwood.ai (443), telemetry.redwood.ai (443).
   - Open egress to artifact storage IP ranges (we listed them in the runbook). No inbound rules required to the node unless you request SSH jumpbox.
   - If you require strict egress control, we'll provide a CIDR list for allowlisting.
3) KMS & Secrets
   - Confirm whether you want Redwood to use customer-managed keys (CMK) or Redwood-managed. For CMK we'll need encrypter/decrypter perms on a specific key.
4) Observability & Ops access
   - Optionally provide a read-only service account for telemetry to send logs to your collector (we support envoy/agent patterns).
   - Indicate if you require audit log forwarding to your Splunk/ELK.
5) Compliance evidence
   - Provide SOC2 / Security questionnaire answers and any required network topology screenshots.
6) Procurement & Scheduling
   - PO or SOW signature; target go-live window (2–4 weeks from intake depending on approvals).

Kickoff goals (45–60m): confirm roles, finalize runbook fields, validate network diagram, agree on CMK approach, and schedule the staging smoke-run.

Next steps:
- Aaron: populate the runbook with the service account name and subnet IDs, and confirm CMK preference.
- Ben (cc'd): I'll loop you in on the runbook where we ask for the artifact CIDRs and egress list — please add specific artifact IP ranges.
- Kimberly (cc'd): can you confirm the expected SLA options and whether Clearfield will require Dedicated capacity SLAs or just hosted-with-vpc for pilot?

If those look good, I'll propose two time slots for the kickoff (Wed 8/19 10:00–11:00 or Thu 8/20 14:00–15:00 PT).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this rolling.

-Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Markus / Aaron — quick notes from the infra side to avoid back-and-forth on the call:

- Artifact downloads: our artifact registry uses a small dynamic range; I'll paste the CIDRs into the runbook before the call. For pilot you can allow egress to artifacts.redwood.ai (443) and we'll provide the IP set if your firewall requires it.
- SSH: we prefer customers not open SSH to nodes. If Clearfield needs shell access for troubleshooting, we'll request a temporary bastion-provided jumpbox with time-limited keys.
- Bandwidth: start with 200 Mbps burstable; for concurrency expect ~100 connections for model downloads during initial seeding. We'll provide telemetry delta after the staging run.
- KMS: CMK is supported — one thing to confirm is whether Clearfield wants rotated keys (if yes, plan for a 30-day rotation ops note).

Also tagging Kimberly for SLA guidance.

Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
